text: Sider holds that the fundamental predicates, like those of physics, 'carve nature at its ___', picking out genuinely natural, mind-independent features of reality.
explanation: Sider's realism about structure holds that some predicates (mass, charge, spin) carve nature at its joints while others (grue, bleen) do not, and that this naturalness is mind-independent. Deflationists reply that 'more natural' may mean only 'more useful for our purposes' rather than tracking objective structure.
